1	# AI Persona Builder
     2	
     3	Build AI persona instruction files for **VS Code Chat**, **Claude Code** and **LangGraph Deep Agents** from YAML metadata and Markdown templates — with zero configuration friction.
     4	
     5	Define your personas once as simple YAML + Markdown sources, and the library generates correctly formatted instruction files for both IDEs. A plugin system lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or post-process output without touching the core engine.
     6	
     7	## ✨ Features
     8	
     9	- **Multi-target output** — generates VS Code `.agent.md`, Claude Code `.md`, Deep Agents `.md`, and any custom format from a single source
    10	- **Extensible target registry** — register custom targets via `TargetRegistry` without touching core code; each target declares its own output key, frontmatter template, and context flags
    11	- **YAML + Markdown templating** — separate metadata from content; merge them at build time with `{{variables}}`, `{{> partials}}`, and `{{#if}}` conditionals
    12	- **Shared + per-suite partials** — reuse content fragments across personas with local overrides
    13	- **Plugin architecture** — hook into context building, post-rendering, validation, and frontmatter generation
    14	- **CI-friendly** — `--check` mode renders without writing; `--strict` exits non-zero on warnings
    15	- **Programmatic & CLI** — use the `build()` API in scripts or run `persona-build` from the command line
    16	- **Single dependency** — only `js-yaml` at runtime
    17	
    18	## 📋 Requirements
    19	
    20	- **Node.js** ≥ 18
    21	
    22	## 🚀 Quick Start
    23	
    24	```bash
    25	npm install @mistralys/persona-builder
    26	```
    27	
    28	- View on NPM: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mistralys/persona-builder
    29	- View on Github: https://github.com/Mistralys/ai-persona-builder
    30	
    31	### Programmatic API
    32	
    33	```ts
    34	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
    35	import path from 'node:path';
    36	
    37	const summary = await build({
    38	  suites: {
    39	    'my-suite': {
    40	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
    41	      outputDirs: {
    42	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
    43	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
    44	      },
    45	    },
    46	  },
    47	  sharedPartialsDir: path.resolve('./personas/shared/partials'),
    48	});
    49	
    50	console.log(`Built ${summary.totalBuilt} persona(s), wrote ${summary.totalWritten} file(s).`);
    51	```
    52	
    53	### CLI
    54	
    55	```bash
    56	# Create a persona-build.config.js, then:
    57	npx persona-build
    58	
    59	# CI staleness check
    60	npx persona-build --check --strict
    61	```
    62	
    63	See the [CLI docs](docs/cli.md) for config file format and all flags.
    64	
    65	## 📖 Documentation
    66	
    67	**Guides** — conceptual and procedural reading:
    68	
    69	| Guide | Description |
    70	|-------|-------------|
    71	| [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md) | Step-by-step tutorial — build your first persona from scratch |
    72	| [Directory Convention](docs/directory-convention.md) | Expected source layout (`meta/`, `content/`, `partials/`) |
    73	| [Template Syntax](docs/template-syntax.md) | Variables, partials, conditionals, and built-in context variables |
    74	| [Plugins](docs/plugins.md) | `PersonaBuildPlugin` interface and examples |
    75	
    76	**Reference** — look-up material:
    77	
    78	| Reference | Description |
    79	|-----------|-------------|
    80	| [Metadata Reference](docs/metadata-reference.md) | All recognized YAML metadata fields, tiers, and fallback rules |
    81	| [Configuration Reference](docs/configuration.md) | `BuildConfig`, `SuiteConfig`, and `BuildSummary` fields |
    82	| [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Command-line flags, config file format, and common patterns |
    83	| [Public API](docs/api.md) | All exported types and functions |
    84	| [Project Manifest](docs/agents/project-manifest/README.md) | Canonical documentation for AI agent sessions |
    85	
    86	## 🔌 Plugins
    87	
    88	The library ships with a plugin system that lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or
    89	post-process output without touching the core engine. See [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) for
    90	the `PersonaBuildPlugin` interface, examples, and the available hooks.
    91	
    92	> **Ledger plugin:** The first-party ledger plugin was migrated out of this library in v2.0.0 and
    93	> is now maintained in the [ai-insights](https://github.com/mistralys/ai-insights-dev) workspace.
    94	> The `@mistralys/persona-builder/plugins/ledger` sub-path export no longer exists.
    95	
    96	---
    97	
    98	## 📄 License
    99	
   100	MIT

1	# Plugins
     2	
     3	Plugins extend the build pipeline without modifying the core engine. Register plugins via `BuildConfig.plugins`.
     4	
     5	## PersonaBuildPlugin Interface
     6	
     7	```ts
     8	interface PersonaBuildPlugin {
     9	  /** Unique name used for logging and identification */
    10	  name: string;
    11	
    12	  /**
    13	   * Called once per suite before any persona is built.
    14	   * Use this to read shared metadata and set up plugin state.
    15	   */
    16	  onSuiteInit?(suite: SuiteConfig, sharedMeta: Record<string, unknown>): void;
    17	
    18	  /**
    19	   * Called for each persona before template rendering.
    20	   * Mutate and return the context to inject additional template variables.
    21	   * The optional `target` parameter indicates the active build target.
    22	   */
    23	  onBuildContext?(
    24	    context: Record<string, unknown>,
    25	    persona: PersonaMetadata,
    26	    suite: SuiteConfig,
    27	    target?: TargetType,
    28	  ): Record<string, unknown>;
    29	
    30	  /**
    31	   * Called after the full output is rendered.
    32	   * Mutate and return the output string (e.g. to append a footer).
    33	   */
    34	  onPostRender?(output: string, persona: PersonaMetadata, target: TargetType): string;
    35	
    36	  /**
    37	   * Called during the validation phase.
    38	   * Return an array of ValidationResult entries (empty = no issues).
    39	   */
    40	  onValidate?(persona: PersonaMetadata, suite: SuiteConfig, target?: TargetType): ValidationResult[];
    41	
    42	  /**
    43	   * Register custom frontmatter templates, keyed by target type.
    44	   * These override the library defaults and config-level overrides.
    45	   */
    46	  frontmatterTemplates?: Partial<Record<TargetType, string>>;
    47	}
    48	```
    49	
    50	## Examples
    51	
    52	### Adding a custom frontmatter field
    53	
    54	```ts
    55	import { build, type PersonaBuildPlugin } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
    56	
    57	const timestampPlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
    58	  name: 'timestamp',
    59	
    60	  onBuildContext(context) {
    61	    // Inject a build-time variable that templates can use as {{build_date}}
    62	    return { ...context, build_date: new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10) };
    63	  },
    64	};
    65	
    66	const summary = await build({
    67	  suites: {
    68	    docs: {
    69	      srcDir: './personas/docs',
    70	      outputDirs: {
    71	        vscode: './dist/vscode',
    72	        'claude-code': './dist/cc',
    73	      },
    74	    },
    75	  },
    76	  plugins: [timestampPlugin],
    77	});
    78	```
    79	
    80	### Custom frontmatter template via plugin
    81	
    82	```ts
    83	const customFrontmatter: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
    84	  name: 'custom-frontmatter',
    85	
    86	  frontmatterTemplates: {

    93	mcpServers:

    96	  },
    97	};

1	# Configuration Reference
     2	
     3	## BuildConfig
     4	
     5	The configuration object passed to `build()`.
     6	
     7	| Field | Type | Default | Description |
     8	|-------|------|---------|-------------|
     9	| `suites` | `Record<string, SuiteConfig>` | **required** | Map of suite names to suite configurations. |
    10	| `sharedPartialsDir` | `string` | `undefined` | Absolute path to a shared partials directory. Partials here are loaded as the base layer; suite-local partials overlay them. |
    11	| `plugins` | `PersonaBuildPlugin[]` | `[]` | Plugins applied to every suite in registration order. |
    12	| `targets` | `string[]` | See below | Output targets to generate. The default is derived from the registry: all targets where `defaultEnabled !== false`. For `defaultRegistry`, this yields `['vscode', 'claude-code']` (the `'deep-agents'` target has `defaultEnabled: false`). Pass an explicit array to override. |
    13	| `check` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true`, personas are rendered but **no files are written**. Useful for CI staleness checks. |
    14	| `strict` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true`, the build throws if any `ValidationResult` has severity `'error'` or `'warning'`. |
    15	| `frontmatter` | `Record<string, string>` | Registry defaults | Override the default frontmatter templates, keyed by target name. See [template syntax](template-syntax.md). |
    16	| `targetRegistry` | `TargetRegistry` | `defaultRegistry` | Registry of target definitions to use for this build. When provided, overrides `defaultRegistry` for output directory resolution, filename lookup, frontmatter defaults, and context flag injection. Register custom targets here to extend the build system. |
    17	
    18	## SuiteConfig
    19	
    20	Per-suite configuration nested inside `BuildConfig.suites`.
    21	
    22	| Field | Type | Default | Description |
    23	|-------|------|---------|-------------|
    24	| `srcDir` | `string` | **required** | Absolute or relative path to the suite source directory. |
    25	| `outVscode` | `string` | `undefined` | _(Deprecated)_ Output directory for VS Code persona files. Use `outputDirs['vscode']` instead; that takes precedence when present. Will be removed in a future major version. |
    26	| `outClaudeCode` | `string` | `undefined` | _(Deprecated)_ Output directory for Claude Code persona files. Use `outputDirs['claude-code']` instead; that takes precedence when present. Will be removed in a future major version. |
    27	| `outputDirs` | `Record<string, string>` | `undefined` | Map of output directories keyed by each target's `outputDirKey` (see note below). Takes precedence over the deprecated fields. Required for the `'deep-agents'` built-in and all custom targets. |
    28	| `personaMode` | `string` | `undefined` | Passthrough value exposed to plugins. The core library does nothing with it; its meaning is entirely plugin-defined. Use it to vary plugin behaviour per suite (e.g. apply different rendering logic when `personaMode === 'ledger'` vs `personaMode === 'standalone'`). Plugins can read it inside `onSuiteInit` and `onBuildContext` via `suite.personaMode`. |
    29	| `partialsSubdir` | `string` | `'partials'` | Sub-directory within `srcDir` containing suite-local partials. |
    30	| `metaSubdir` | `string` | `'meta'` | Sub-directory within `srcDir` containing YAML metadata files. |
    31	| `contentSubdir` | `string` | `'content'` | Sub-directory within `srcDir` containing Markdown content templates. |
    32	
    33	> **`outputDirs` key note:** Each key in `outputDirs` must match the target's `outputDirKey` field (declared in its `TargetDefinition`), **not** necessarily the target name. For the three built-in targets `outputDirKey` equals the target name (`'vscode'`, `'claude-code'`, `'deep-agents'`), so there is no difference in practice. For a custom target where `outputDirKey` differs from `name`, use the `outputDirKey` value as the map key.
    34	
    35	## BuildSummary
    36	
    37	The object returned by `build()`.
    38	
    39	| Field | Type | Description |
    40	|-------|------|-------------|
    41	| `success` | `boolean` | `true` unless strict mode is on and there are validation failures. |
    42	| `results` | `BuildResult[]` | One entry per persona × target combination. |
    43	| `strictFailures` | `ValidationResult[]` | Validation issues that triggered a strict-mode failure. |
    44	| `totalBuilt` | `number` | Total number of persona × target combinations processed. |
    45	| `totalWritten` | `number` | Number of output files actually written to disk (0 in check mode). |

1	# Template Syntax
     2	
     3	Templates use a lightweight `{{…}}` syntax with no external dependencies.
     4	
     5	## Variables
     6	
     7	```
     8	{{variableName}}
     9	```
    10	
    11	Values are sourced from the merged context (shared YAML + per-persona YAML + plugin `onBuildContext`). Missing variables emit a warning to stderr but do not fail the build.
    12	
    13	## Partials
    14	
    15	```
    16	{{> partialName}}
    17	```
    18	
    19	Partials are loaded from the `partials/` directory and resolved up to 2 levels deep.
    20	
    21	## Conditionals
    22	
    23	```
    24	{{#if flagName}}
    25	Content shown when flagName is truthy.
    26	{{else}}
    27	Fallback content.
    28	{{/if}}
    29	```
    30	
    31	### Else-If Chains
    32	
    33	Use `{{else if flagName}}` to express multi-branch conditionals without deep nesting:
    34	
    35	```
    36	{{#if a}}
    37	Content shown when a is truthy.
    38	{{else if b}}
    39	Content shown when a is falsy and b is truthy.
    40	{{else}}
    41	Fallback content when both a and b are falsy.
    42	{{/if}}
    43	```
    44	
    45	**Truth table:**
    46	
    47	| `a` | `b` | Output |
    48	|-----|-----|--------|
    49	| `true` | any | first branch |
    50	| `false` | `true` | second branch |
